newsitem.title: UK: Spain leads bond markets in bullish week - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Spain leads bond markets in bullish week - Salomon.

text.p: Spanish bonds gave investors the best return during what was a bullish week for all major bond markets, data from Salomon Brothers showed on Friday.

Spanish Bonos returned 1.51 percent in peseta terms, well ahead of the second best performer, Sweden, which made a 0.93 percent gain. All 16 markets in Salomon's main bond index were in positive territory, with the overall index up 0.49 percent. Spanish bonds, also best peformer in the year so far with a 13.40 percent return, surged in the week amid optimism Spain would produce a relatively tight budget, low inflation figures, and expectations Spanish interest rates would be cut soon.
The Bank of Spain governor said earlier in the week that a strict 1997 budget would make room for a possible rate move.
The Australian market, which was third best performer, similarly was buoyed by expectations of another interest rate cut by year end on the back of a weak labour market.
Australian bonds returned 0.85 percent in local currency terms. Meanwhile, the yield gap between Australian and U.S. bonds narrowed to its lowest level in two years during the week.

But other dollar bloc markets, while performing well, lagged. Canadian bonds came in last with a 0.18 percent return and U.S. Treasuries were next-worst with 0.24 percent. In U.S. dollar terms, Spanish bonds also proved profitable, giving a 1.69 percent return, second only to Sweden which returned 1.75 percent. Again, all of the markets gave positive returns in dollar terms. Australia showed the weakest gains with 0.05 percent.
Japanese government bonds were in the middle of the pack in yen terms, returning 0.61 percent, but were near the top in dollar terms with a 1.26 percent return.
The other benchmark market, Bunds, was near the low end of the list in both categories. They had a 0.39 percent return in marks and a 0.28 percent gain in dollar terms.

Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest.
